summary: Resumed WP4-A. The previous builder had left a nearly complete package on disk: sports/odds.py (role 11), sports/gamestate.py (role 12), 23 tests, labelled fixtures, both reports and the raw smoke data. I kept all of it and re-checked every AC against the dispatch, the contracts and the Phase 1 conventions. I found and fixed one safety defect. `gamestate.feed_age_ms` reported the `sports` feed age as the FRESHEST feed, which fails open: the Polymarket WS stays "fresh" on other sports' messages even if ESPN polling dies. It now follows the convention in trader/marketdata.py for "polymarket": `sports` is the OLDEST of the expected feeds, and it is absent until each of them has reported, so the kernel sees it as stale. The test was updated to cover this. I also added a `ponytail:` comment on Quota.take: there is no file lock between processes. I did not redo the smoke run or download any data again. The existing smoke report (2026-10-01 09:20 to 09:43 UTC) matches the raw files on disk (kalshi 149 lines, espn 25, polymarket-sports 53 frames over 68.5 s). The quota report regenerates byte-identical. 23/23 tests pass.

key_results: 23/23 tests pass. Code change this session: gamestate.feed_age_ms(now_ms, feeds=("espn","polymarket-ws")) now returns {"sports:<feed>": age, "sports": the oldest of feeds}, and leaves out "sports" until every feed has reported. Before, it took the freshest feed, which failed open. WP4-B's sports/pulls.py already reads the "sports" key with a 120 s bound, so it gets the fail-closed value. Quota projection (SportsGameOdds, 2,500/month, 3 snapshots per event): all 5 leagues are enabled; peak-month total is 30.5% of quota (E0 198, SP1 150, D1 126, I1 174, F1 114 units). Smoke run: Kalshi 48 events with full H/D/A probs; ESPN 48 games (all scheduled); WS 53 frames in 75 s with no soccer live at the time; 144/144 crawler moneyline rows mapped; 0 cancel signals.
wiring_notes: The recorder process runs sports.odds.kalshi_snapshots(), sgo_snapshots() and oddsapi_snapshots(), all sharing one sports.odds.Quota(data/sports/quota.json); news refreshes pass priority="news". For each mapped event it calls odds.due(start_ms, lineup_ms, done_labels, now) and records the returned labels in done_labels. It runs gamestate.poll_espn(league) every 30-60 s near kickoff, and runs gamestate.listen_ws(seconds, on_state) inside a reconnect loop (listen_ws raises on disconnect). OddsSnapshot and GameState dicts are appended to data/sports/. trader/marketdata.py builds sports MarketInfo from odds.map_markets(crawler_rows, espn_states + kalshi_snapshots); MarketMap.event_key is the event_group / cluster id. On every GameState update the loop calls sig = gamestate.cancel_signal(gs, maps, now), and if sig, gamestate.cancel_game(sig, paper_router, now). marketdata.feed_age_ms merges gamestate.feed_age_ms(now); pass feeds=("espn",) if the WS is not run, otherwise "sports" never appears and the kernel treats it as stale. nightly/report.py can call odds.project_quota() and odds.Quota().used(source) for the quota section. football-data closing_odds() is for CLV only, never for quoting.
open_issues: A11 [ops]: the SportsGameOdds and odds-api.io response shapes are mock fixtures built from public docs. Verify them against a live response once keys exist (env SPORTSGAMEODDS_API_KEY, ODDS_API_IO_KEY).

The soccer WS parser has only been tested on soccer-shaped frames. During the 75 s smoke no soccer game was live, so frames with leagueAbbreviation epl/lal/bun/sea/fl1 were never captured. Capture some during a match day and check the soccer status strings. Unknown statuses already fail closed to 'suspended'.
Kalshi kickoff is taken as occurrence_datetime minus 3h, based on what was observed on 2026-10-01. It held for 48/48 events in the smoke, but would have to change if Kalshi changes the field.
WS GameState event_key uses the receive date (the feed has no scheduled start), so a game that crosses UTC midnight would not match its MarketMap. A ponytail comment marks this.
Quota.take has no inter-process file lock (a ponytail comment marks this); one collector process should own data/sports/quota.json.
A newer crawler snapshot (2026-10-01T121820Z.jsonl) exists. The smoke mapped the earlier snapshot from the same day (08:49Z), which still meets A9's 'today's crawler rows'.
